rationale: Both normalise the text, size the rectangle and read it down the columns with the same loop. A keeps only Unicode letters and digits, but then indexes the result byte by byte (msg[i], WriteByte). Any non-ASCII letter would be split into broken bytes, so A's filter and its output disagree. B stores the message as runes and writes runes, so it handles that case correctly. B also has a clear doc comment, which A lacks. A's integer search for c avoids floating point, and its padding is done inline more simply than B's append-then-fill step, which is slightly clunky. Even so, B's correct handling of non-ASCII text and its documentation make it the better code overall.
